gcd(r,s)=gcd(p,q),

and, whenever |r|+|s|>2, another pair r′,s′∈T satisfying

gcd(r′,s′)=gcd(r,s),   |r′|+|s′|<|r|+|s|.

The same construction applied after replacing r,s by r−2,s−2 preserves the second gcd. Thus the two hypotheses imply that the descent terminates with two elements whose gcds, before and after subtracting 2, are both 1. The only terminal pair is {0,1} up to order and simultaneous sign; hence 0,1∈T.

Once 0,1∈T, induction gives every integer. Indeed, if n∈T, then 1−n=1²−n∈T. Hence T is closed under n↦1−n. Starting with 0 and 1, this yields −1 and 2; applying the same operation alternately yields all integers. Therefore T=Z. ∎

Apply the lemma to T=S and the elements a,b supplied by (a). Its hypotheses are exactly (a), while its closure hypothesis is (b). Consequently S=Z.
